name: mine
comment: Mines the replay buffer every other arm reads. One update-free refresh epoch:
it samples the frozen base policy, scores each candidate and writes
<output_dir>/<stamp>_mine/replay_buffer. No optimizer or EMA step happens, so
the buffer belongs to the checkpoint it started from -- re-mine whenever that
checkpoint changes, and never delete a finished one to save disk, because
reproducing it costs the full mine again.
start_epoch == epochs is what makes this a mine and not a training epoch; the
config's hdp_rollout_interval decides which epochs are allowed to be one
(start_epoch - 1 must be a multiple of it).
Point the arm's resume_replay_root at the buffer this writes.
The four candidate-weighting flags below are dropped rather than set: guided
enrichment scores its candidates group-relative, so candidate-0 behaviour-anchor
semantics are not available while mining and the trainer refuses the combination.
The arm applies them at replay time instead, which is the whole point of caching
rewards rather than weights -- one buffer serves any weighting rule.
